strategy: Independent fresh paintings, using the original Day 1 only for character and style. Day 22 additionally uses the equipment plate solely for trap geometry. No generated revision is used as another scene's reference.

images.scene: Removing the single small fish through the opened rear access of the willow cage at the safe river margin.
images.prompt: Paint a NEW wide 16:9 watercolour and fine brown ink survival illustration on warm ivory paper. Reference 1 supplies ONLY the lean man's identity (about 30, ear-length dark wavy hair, short beard), autumn valley palette and hand-painted style. Reference 2 supplies ONLY fishing-cage geometry; do NOT copy its typography, cutaway, missing wall or blueprint style. Fresh composition, no writing. Broad clean ochre skin washes, ink on outer contours, no repetitive skin hatching. Northern Iberia about 40,000 calibrated BP, early autumn, small safe shallow river margin with grey stones and golden woodland. CLOSE THREE-QUARTER VIEW: the man crouches on dry stones, has lifted a small willow fish cage onto the bank, and gently draws ONE small silvery fish out THROUGH ITS OPEN REAR ACCESS END. Fish about finger-length, not a large trout. Cage is a forearm-length cylindrical woven willow basket, fully intact woven side walls. At LEFT/front end there is a wide circular mouth with an inward tapered woven entrance funnel narrowing INSIDE the body. At RIGHT/rear end near his hands the round removable woven access cap has been untied and placed beside the cylinder; his hand and the fish emerge from this full-width OPEN REAR access, NOT the narrow entrance funnel. Make the two ends and this retrieval operation unambiguous. Tether line remains loosely attached to a small anchor stone. Natural nettle lashings, no metal wire or plastic. Show enough foreground space around open end and detached cap for their shape to read. Bare feet, overlapping opaque bark waist panels and SMALL fitted rabbit-fur pelvic pad with bark ties. Upper body mostly bare; limited old bark shoulder screen may show, NO fox fur yet. No shelter, fire, Neanderthals, tools invented later or pot. Calm careful action with alert posture. Dissolved paper margins and luminous earthy transparent washes.

images.scene: Backing away from a warning spear after the spindle demonstration fails to secure a welcome.
images.prompt:
Paint a NEW wide watercolour-and-fine-brown-ink story illustration on warm ivory paper, 16:9. Original reference fixes ONLY the traveller's face and style: lean man about 30, dark wavy ear-length hair, short beard. Broad clean skin washes and contour ink. Northern Iberia, 40,000 calibrated BP, early autumn, open rocky ground with scattered golden trees OUTSIDE the neighbours' camp. A frightened traveller at left steps urgently backwards with empty visible hands. Bark waist panels, small rabbit-fur pelvic pad, NARROW reddish-grey fox-fur strip over his anatomical LEFT shoulder, mostly bare chest. At right, several paces away, ONE upright NEANDERTHAL adult man warns him back with a plain wooden spear held diagonally across the space. Make this Neanderthal's PROFILE LARGE AND READABLE: low receding forehead, massive continuous brow ridge, strongly projecting midface and broad substantial nose, distinctly weak receding chin. Compact robust human body and relatively short forearms and shins, competent natural posture, simple practical hide wraps. A clear anatomical contrast with the lean modern traveller's pronounced chin. Not a sapiens in fur, not an ape or stooped caricature. Other locals outside crop. The first small wooden spindle lies abandoned beside a stone between them, modest loose yarn beside it. No wound, handshake, teaching or gift accepted. Traveller still withdrawing, not attacking. No atlatl, permanent building, metal, fantasy jewellery or writing. Human nuance: wary local warning, frightened outsider, distance and retreat visible. Luminous earth-colour washes, grey rocks, warm paper edges.
CRITICAL SPEAR MATERIAL: the local man's weapon is a PLAIN ONE-PIECE WOODEN SPEAR. Its point is tapered sharpened WOOD continuous with the shaft, same brown wood grain, NO separate stone, flint or metal head, NO bindings, socket or lashing near the point. Make the continuous wooden taper visibly clear. A wood point matches this exact warning scene. Neanderthal profile: heavy brow and low receding forehead, projecting central midface, substantial nose, weak chin; upright human proportions and competent stance.

images.scene: Rebinding the knife at his own camp after retreat, with the plain wooden spear within reach.
images.prompt: Paint a NEW wide 16:9 watercolour and fine brown ink story illustration on warm ivory paper. Use reference 1 ONLY for the lean traveller's identity (about thirty, dark wavy ear-length hair and short beard), original autumn palette and style. New camera composition and clean broad ochre skin washes, ink mainly outer contours; no accumulated repetitive skin hatching. Northern Iberia fictional valley around 40,000 calibrated BP, early autumn. Day 26 AFTER a frightening rebuffed visit, traveller ALONE back at his OWN camp. Close three-quarter waist-up view from his anatomical LEFT: he sits low on the ground at the small uphill craft spot, carefully retightening a short natural cord binding around a small stone-flake knife in a plain wood handle. Knife palm-length, no metal blade. Expression thoughtful and wary, gaze briefly toward woodland beyond crop. A plain wooden spear with an integral sharpened wooden end lies within easy reach to the side, clearly visible but unobtrusive, NOT stone-tipped. He has opaque bark waist panels and a small rabbit-fur pelvic pad. A NARROW reddish-grey fox-fur panel, only hand-span wide and forearm long, remains on his LEFT shoulder (image-right in this camera), with two simple bark ties and limited old bark screen beneath edge; most chest and opposite shoulder exposed. Background left softly shows edge of SAME low bark-and-leaf debris shelter beneath thick mossy FALLEN LIMB, at drained terrace above river. No stone table, house or new raised rack; ordinary outside hearth is downhill and outside frame, no fire at shelter. No other people, spindle, whorl demonstration, atlatl, darts, feathers or gifts. This scene is retreat and equipment maintenance, no successful communal lesson. Earthy transparent washes, warm paper margins, precise small tools, readable natural hands, no text.

images.scene: A continuous cord fixed eye tied as an overhand loop on a bight, with the running line threaded through it to make the adjustable loop.
images.prompt: Draw a NEW precise 1950s practical manual illustration in navy ink and pale honey/sage pastel on ivory paper. Wide landscape. Title SNARE LINE — FIXED EYE. Two large clean panels. LEFT: a genuine overhand loop knot tied ON A BIGHT of one continuous thin twisted natural cord, enlarged for visibility: small elongated terminal eye above a compact DOUBLED overhand knot; short tail and long standing part below. Clear over-under crossings. Labels FIXED EYE and OVERHAND LOOP KNOT. No detached ring, no metal, no toroidal rope doughnut. RIGHT: draw that same tied eye and knot at top centre. From the knot a long standing part descends, curves into ONE large loose adjustable loop below, rises on the right, passes THROUGH the small terminal eye ONCE, then CONTINUES VISIBLY FAR BEYOND THE EYE toward UPPER LEFT as a long line leaving the panel. The line MUST NOT stop at the eye or merge into the eye. Show at least 15 cm on paper of uninterrupted line AFTER it exits the eye, a separate clear outgoing line travelling left-up across empty background. Label that visible continuation LINE CONTINUES TO ANCHOR. Label the eye crossing SLIDING RETURN and the large lower loop ADJUSTABLE LOOP. Keep a short knot tail distinct below-left of the knot. All is the SAME cord: tied fixed eye -> knot -> long line around large loop -> through eye -> continuing freely towards anchor. Thin cord outlines with white gaps at undercrossings, flattened readable technical drawing rather than photorealistic fat rope. Small sage arrow beside sliding strand. No spring installation, hands, animal, metal, rope pile or extra knots. Correct topology and fully traceable line take precedence over decorative texture. Sparse clear uppercase lettering and generous margins.
